concept.name: Downtrend
concept.definition: A trend characterized by a series of descending peaks and troughs — successively lower highs and lower lows. It is the classical chart-based description of sustained supply exceeding demand; an analytical construct, not evidence that prices must keep falling.
concept.intuition: Each rally stalls lower than the last and each drop breaks to a new floor — a staircase descending.
concept.mechanics: Identified when each successive swing high forms below the prior swing high and each successive swing low breaks below the prior swing low. Often visualized with a down trendline connecting two or more falling highs; the downtrend is conventionally considered intact while price stays below that line or the last lower high.
concept.failure_modes: Counter-trend rallies within downtrends can be sharp and prolonged, and are indistinguishable from genuine reversals until the structure confirms one way or the other.
concept.misconceptions: That a downtrend means every bounce should be shorted immediately; bear-market rallies can retrace large portions of a decline before the downtrend resumes.
concept.example: A stock falls from 100 to 90, bounces to 95, then falls to 88: lower highs (100, 95) and lower lows (90, 88) mark a downtrend.
